h1: The 6 Best CREWORKS Ultrasonic Cleaners of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best CREWORKS Ultrasonic Cleaner: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 CREWORKS ultrasonic cleaners from a 2L bench tub to a 30L shop tank, scored on watts per liter, heating and tank size.
summary: The CREWORKS 6L Digital with 180W is the one to buy for most homes: enough tank for tools and eyewear, a drain valve, and a clean 20 to 80C range. Step up to the 10L when you clean in batches, or the 15L for long parts. The 3.2L knob unit is the best small-tank value, and the 2L suits a few rings and a pair of glasses.
intro: The CREWORKS line looks like a simple size ladder, 2 liters up to 30, but the power does not scale evenly. The 6L delivers about 30 watts of ultrasonic energy per liter, while the 15L and 30L deliver closer to 24 and 20. A bigger tank is not a stronger cleaner, and shops that buy the biggest tub for a modest job often get weaker cavitation than a smaller unit would give.

We ranked six CREWORKS machines on the Primea framework, weighting watts per liter, heating wattage, timer and drain design. The numbers come from each spec sheet, and the verdicts compare models inside the same brand so you can pick the right rung of the ladder rather than the longest one.

products.name: CREWORKS 6L Digital Ultrasonic Cleaner, 180W 40kHz
products.verdict: The sweet spot of the line: 6 liters, 180W, a drain valve and a real temperature range.
products.description:
This 6-liter model pairs 180W at 40 kHz with a 304 stainless tank and a heater spanning 20 to 80C (68 to 176F). A 1 to 30 minute timer and a built-in drain valve complete the controls. At roughly 30 watts per liter it has the densest ultrasonic output of the larger tanks here.

It beats the 10L because small to medium jobs do not need the extra water, and it beats the 3.2L knob unit by fitting tools and bicycle parts that overflow a smaller tub. The trade is price: it sits at $100 to $200, higher than the 2L and 3.2L machines.

Best for a household that cleans eyewear, hardware, kitchen gadgets and sturdy jewelry on the same machine. The caveat is the 80C ceiling, which is fine for most work but short of what greasy engine parts prefer.
pros: Best watts per liter among large tanks
products.idealFor: Households wanting one machine for glasses, hardware and sturdy jewelry.
products.skipIf: You only clean a few small items at a time.

products.name: CREWORKS 10L Digital Ultrasonic Cleaner, 240W
products.verdict: Ten liters and up to 300W of heat make batch cleaning of engine and kitchen parts practical.
products.description:
The 10L adds capacity without adding much complexity: 240W of ultrasonic power, up to 300W of heating, a 20 to 80C range and a drain valve. It handles carburetor sets, bike chains and a rack of kitchen gadgets in one go.

It ranks below the 6L because the ultrasonic density drops to roughly 24 watts per liter, so tough dirt takes longer to release. It ranks above the 15L because the lighter footprint is easier to fit on a bench, and the 300W heater reaches working temperature quickly.

Choose it if you clean hobby parts in batches. Skip it if your largest item fits in a 6-liter tank, since the extra solution costs more to fill and dispose of without improving results.
cons: Lower watts per liter than the 6L
More solution to buy and dispose
products.idealFor: Hobbyists and DIYers cleaning engine, bike and kitchen parts in batches.
products.skipIf: Your biggest part fits comfortably in a 6-liter tank.

products.name: CREWORKS 3.2L Ultrasonic Cleaner, 120W with Knobs
products.verdict: The highest watts per liter in the line, with simple two-knob control and a mid-small tank.
products.description:
A 3.2L tank measuring 10.8 x 7.2 x 8.9 inches, 120W of cavitation and a 100W heater that runs from 70 to 175F. Two knobs handle time and temperature, up to 30 minutes. That works out to nearly 38 watts per liter, the strongest ratio of any CREWORKS here.

The design helps jewelry, watches and small tools where dense cavitation matters more than volume. It trails the 6L because longer parts such as wrenches and chains will not lay flat, and the knobs give no exact readout. It beats the 2L by holding more at once and heating faster with the same 100W heater.

Buy it for a desk or kitchen-counter cleaner at $50 to $100. The caveat is the missing digital display, so repeating a setting means remembering where the dial sat.
products.idealFor: People cleaning jewelry, watches, glasses and small tools on a counter.
products.skipIf: You need a drain or want to repeat exact settings.

products.name: CREWORKS 15L Digital Ultrasonic Cleaner, 360W
products.verdict: A 15-liter tank for long parts and big batches, at the same 24 watts per liter as the 10L.
products.description:
Fifteen liters (4 gallons) with 360W of ultrasonic power, a 20 to 80C range, a 1 to 30 minute timer and a built-in drain valve. The tank is large enough for fuel rails, long tool sets and a stack of baskets.

It ranks fourth because most households never fill a tank this size, and the density of cavitation is the same 24 watts per liter as the 10L. It ranks above the 30L since the 15L fits a normal workbench and costs $100 to $200 instead of $200 to $500.

Buy it if you regularly clean parts longer than 10 inches or run two baskets together. The caveat is solution: filling and heating 15 liters is a real cost, and the weight of a full tank makes the drain valve essential.
products.idealFor: Workshop users cleaning long parts or running multiple baskets at once.
products.skipIf: Your parts fit in 6 or 10 liters.

products.name: CREWORKS 2L Digital Ultrasonic Cleaner, 60W 40kHz
products.verdict: A small digital tub for rings, glasses and trinkets, with a 100W heater and two fuses.
products.description:
The smallest CREWORKS: a 2L stainless tank, 60W at 40 kHz, a 100W heater (68 to 176F), a digital panel and two built-in fuses. The tank holds a pair of glasses or a handful of rings, but not a wrench or a watch band laid flat.

At 30 watts per liter it matches the 6L on density, but the absolute power is a third of the 3.2L model's, so stubborn grime takes longer. It ranks below the knob unit because it offers less capacity for the same $50 to $100 bracket, and above the 30L only because the 30L is overbuilt for homes.

Pick it if desk space is tight and the load stays small. The caveat is volume: anything bigger than a pair of sunglasses needs a larger tub.
pros: Good density at 30 W per liter
products.idealFor: Light users cleaning rings, glasses and small items in tight spaces.
products.skipIf: You clean anything longer than a pair of glasses.

products.name: CREWORKS 30L Digital Ultrasonic Cleaner, 600W
products.verdict: A 30-liter, 600W industrial-size tub that only makes sense in a shop.
products.description:
Thirty liters with 600W of ultrasonic power, a matching 600W heater, a 20 to 80C range, a drain valve and a timer up to 30 minutes. It is the only CREWORKS here built for a workshop floor or a heavy bench.

It ranks last for a household buyer because density falls to 20 watts per liter, the weakest in the line, and the price sits at $200 to $500. The 600W heater is the best in the group, which helps fill-and-go shops, but it also means a long warm-up for 30 liters of fluid.

Buy it for a small business or serious shop cleaning large parts in volume. Avoid it for home use: you will fill, heat and drain far more solution than you need.
products.idealFor: Small shops and serious hobbyists cleaning very large parts in volume.
products.skipIf: You are cleaning at home or have limited bench space.

whatMatters.detail: Divide ultrasonic watts by tank liters to see cavitation density. The 6L at 180W gives about 30 watts per liter, the 30L at 600W about 20. Higher density cleans stubborn dirt faster. Check the listing for ultrasonic output, not heater wattage, before judging a large tank.

Volume sets what you can fit, but inside dimensions decide it. The 3.2L tank is 10.8 inches long, which stops short of a socket set or a long wrench. Measure your longest part and compare it with the listed tank length, not only the liters.

A stronger heater means a quicker warm-up, and a higher temperature ceiling means faster oil removal. CREWORKS units run 20 to 80C, with heaters from 100W up to 600W. For small tubs 100W is plenty; for 15 liters and up, look for 300W or more.

Digital panels show exact time and temperature, so a good recipe repeats. Knobs are tactile but vague. The 3.2L uses two knobs, while the 2L, 6L, 10L, 15L and 30L use digital panels. Pick based on whether you value repeatability or simplicity, and note that the knob model also has the smallest tank in the group.

A full 15-liter tank of dirty solution is heavy and messy. A drain valve lets you empty it into a bucket without tipping the machine. The 6L, 10L, 15L and 30L list one; the 2L and 3.2L do not, which is fine at those small volumes but means lifting a wet tub to the sink every time.

faq.q: Do CREWORKS cleaners come with a basket?
faq.a: The spec sheets we reviewed focus on tank, power and heater, so confirm what ships with your listing. For the 6L and larger units a basket matters, because parts should never sit directly on the stainless floor of the tank.

faq.q: What is the common mistake with the 30L model?
faq.a: Buying it because bigger seems better. At about 20 watts per liter the CREWORKS 30L has the thinnest cavitation in the line, and you will fill and heat far more solution than a household needs. The 6L cleans most things faster.

faq.q: Is the 10L worth it over the 6L?
faq.a: Only if you clean batches or longer parts. The 10L adds a 300W heater and 240W output, but its density is lower than the 6L's, so single small items do not clean faster. For everyday glasses and hardware, the 6L wins.

faq.q: How should I set up the tank?
faq.a: Fill with water and cleaning solution to the marked level, never run it empty, and let the heater bring it to working temperature before you load parts. The 6L, 10L and 15L models give 20 to 80C, which suits most jobs.

faq.q: How do I maintain a CREWORKS cleaner?
faq.a: Drain after each heavy session, wipe the 304 stainless to prevent residue, and replace solution when it clouds. The 6L through 30L units have drain valves that make this easy; the 2L and 3.2L you empty by hand.

faq.q: Can the 2L clean a watch band?
faq.a: Not comfortably. A 2L tank is sized for glasses and rings, and a full watch band or bracelet often will not lay flat. The 3.2L at 10.8 inches long is the smallest CREWORKS that handles it, and the 6L does it easily.

finalTake: The CREWORKS 6L Digital Ultrasonic Cleaner, 180W 40kHz is the pick for most buyers because it balances cavitation density, a drain valve and a usable tank. Choose the 10L for batches, the 15L for long parts, and the 3.2L when you want the strongest density in a counter-size tub. The 2L is for tiny loads only. The 30L is a shop tool, not a home appliance.
